fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 cannot make every signed nonpermutation polynomially farther. For any linear Euclidean realization with cheap permutations P1,P2,P3, a signed nonpermutation T=P1+P2-P3 has squared distance at most nine times the common legal squared radius by the triangle inequality; changing the Gram matrix does not escape this constant-factor ceiling.

Proposal 2 supplies neither an explicit selector matrix nor a protected-center cost calculation. Testing whether small hashes isolate matchings does not test the actual obstruction, while the existing global-branch experiment already admits a weight-9 rectangle splice; any proposed escape must specify and attack the complete syndrome fiber.

Proposal 3 is incompatible with binary linearization: three cheap legal fillings XOR to another target-fiber word of weight at most three times the legal cost. Nonabelian labels or Fox derivatives do not prevent this after conversion to a binary boundary matrix; enforcing reduced-word validity nonlinearly would require an unprovided, potentially exponential representation.

Proposal 4 has an implementation trilemma. Whole-path columns enumerate exponentially many assignment paths, edge columns cannot linearly encode noncommutative path products, and flow/tableau enforcement re-enters O2; noncommutative identity testing also preserves nonzeroness rather than Hamming support, the exact failure seen for prior condensers.

Proposal 5 has no polynomial parameter regime: fixed truncation degree is covered by bounded-degree cube relations, while growing degree generally creates n^D Macaulay monomials and becomes superpolynomial before supplying logarithmic/global soundness. The target homology class and precise differential are also unspecified, so the proposed finite computation would not test a complete reduction.

Proposal 6 is not a lattice construction because binomial(z_j,2) is nonlinear in lattice coefficients. Linearizing it with monomial variables either returns to bounded-degree cube cancellations or requires a growing monomial dictionary, while spanning lifted Boolean fiber points requires finding or enumerating the NP-hard fiber.

Proposal 7 has the same affine-combination ceiling as Proposal 1. Three low-cost legal permutation routings linearly combine to a signed nonpermutation routing with squared congestion at most nine times the worst legal cost, and the q log q legal routing baseline already prevents logarithmic replication from producing a polynomial ratio.
evidence: All seven proposals are explicitly marked untested; no supplied verifier establishes any claimed separation for them.

The obstruction map proves bounded-degree signatures, marginal/tableau interfaces, and bounded-fan-in linearizations retain exact short trades, directly covering the fallback implementations in proposals 3–6.

Existing selector evidence found a weight-9 rectangle splice, and affine-closure verification found 32 instances where an illegal cover lies in the affine span of legal matchings. These are concrete warnings against proposals 2 and 3, not asymptotic extrapolations.

Prior noncommutative and dense-fold verifiers preserved orientation or nonzeroness but failed support separation: M3(F4) produced NO kernels, and the F8 condenser had worst YES 31 versus best NO 6. Proposal 4 supplies no theorem or structural mutation addressing that rank-to-support failure.

The direct permutation-table construction already achieved only additive 12 versus 14, and the determinant/all-compound mutation retained short virtual permutations. Proposals 1 and 7 do not escape the underlying linear affine-combination bound.
next_experiment: None for these proposals. Reopen only after supplying an explicit polynomial-size matrix whose columns are computable without enumerating witnesses, together with a proof-level reason that signed combinations of three cheap legal representations cannot yield a cheap target-fiber word; then precommit one exact all-eight, affine-closure, holonomy, and all-mixed-word test.
